Find a Roofing Company in Dallas With One Free Call

Hail last night, a stain spreading on the ceiling, or a roof that is just worn out. Call one number at any hour and you are put through to an independent roofing company that is locally owned and works across Dallas-Fort Worth.

Call (469) 649-7066 See how the line works

A phone line that finds you a Dallas roofer

Typing "roofing company in Dallas" into a search bar returns hundreds of names, ads that look alike, and a lot of door knockers who showed up after the last storm. This site takes a different approach: one free number, answered around the clock, that rings through to a locally owned, independent roofer working in your corner of the metroplex.

DFW Expert Roofers does no roof work itself. It does not inspect, quote, repair or replace anything, and it does not handle insurance claims. Its job is to answer, ask a few quick questions about the roof and your town, and connect you. The roofing company you reach takes it from there: it comes out, finds the problem, prices the job in writing, and you decide whether to hire it.

The rest of this site is here so you know what to ask when that roofer arrives: how hail damage is spotted, what a fair repair quote lists, what your city requires, and what Texas law says about deductibles and storm chasers.

Why roofs wear out fast around Dallas-Fort Worth

North Texas throws nearly every kind of roof weather at a house within a single year. Knowing which one hit yours tells a roofer where to look first.

Spring hail

The worst storms usually arrive between March and June. The May 5, 1995 Mayfest storm dropped softball-size hail on the festival crowd in Fort Worth and its damage across Tarrant and Dallas counties is commonly put at about $2 billion, though the earliest estimates were lower. On June 13, 2012, the National Weather Service in Fort Worth logged hail as large as baseballs and softballs across Dallas and Collin counties, smashing car windows and skylights in North Dallas. Hail bruises shingles and knocks off granules in ways that are hard to see from the yard.

Straight-line wind and tornadoes

Thunderstorm winds can peel ridge caps and crease shingles over whole neighborhoods, and tornadoes have struck the metro many times, including the December 26, 2015 tornado that crossed Sunnyvale, Garland and Rowlett and the EF3 tornado that tore through North Dallas on October 20, 2019. Wind damage often shows up as lifted tabs and missing shingles along edges and ridges.

Summer heat

Long stretches of triple-digit days bake asphalt shingles and dry out sealants around pipes and vents. Attic ventilation matters as much as the shingle itself, and a poorly vented attic can shorten a roof's life.

Ice and freezes

Winter storms are rare but rough. In February 2021 snow, sleet and freezing rain coated the region, and DFW Airport fell to minus 2 degrees on February 16. Ice can back water up under shingles at the eaves, and ice-laden limbs can fall on the roof.

Texas also leads the country in large hail. Citing the Insurance Information Institute, Texas Public Radio reported 902 major hail events (stones an inch across or larger) in Texas in 2025, more than any other state. If a storm has passed over your street, it is worth having a roofer look before the next one does.

What happens when you call

The call takes a couple of minutes. You never pay the line, and you are never obligated to hire anyone.

  1. Dial the lineAn automated assistant picks up (469) 649-7066 any time and asks what you need. The same number also takes air conditioning, heating and pressure washing calls, so say "roof".
  2. Tell it about the roofHail, a drip in the ceiling, shingles in the yard, a tree limb, or an aging roof you want checked, plus your town and how soon you need someone.
  3. Get transferredThe call goes to an independent roofing company that is locally owned and works in Dallas-Fort Worth. It hears a quick summary of your call before it answers.
  4. Work with that companyIt inspects, prices and does the job, and you pay it (or your insurer does, as you arrange). If it cannot pick up, it gets your name, number, town and need so it can call you back.

After the roofer looks at the roof

You should get a written estimate that lists what will be removed and installed, the shingle or panel product, how the decking and flashing will be handled, cleanup, the permit if your city needs one, and the warranty terms. With a claim, you deal with your insurer directly. The roofer may point out damage to the adjuster, yet it has no standing to bargain over the claim.

Take the time you need. A good roofer will not pressure you to sign on the spot, especially after a hailstorm when crews from out of town are knocking on doors.

Not sure if this is a small repair, an insurance claim or the end of the roof? Call and describe it in your own words. The DFW roofing company you are connected with sees the roof in person and puts its estimate in writing before anyone starts work.

Five things to settle before you sign with any roofer

  1. Insurance you can confirm. Have the roofer's insurance agent send you a general liability certificate directly, and call the agent if anything looks off.
  2. The permit question. Many DFW cities, Plano and Dallas among them, require a permit for a re-roof, and some require roofers to register with the city. Ask who pulls the permit and get the number.
  3. A complete written contract. Scope, materials by brand and line, decking price per sheet, start date, cleanup, payment schedule and warranty, with no blank spaces.
  4. No deductible games. State law bars any contractor from waiving, refunding or absorbing a deductible. An offer to do so is a reason to call someone else.
  5. Payment tied to progress. Keep most of the money back at the start, and release the last payment only for a finished job with invoice and warranty in hand.

What Dallas-Fort Worth callers ask first

Is DFW Expert Roofers a roofing company?

Not at all: just a free number plus this website. Nobody here climbs, prices, sells shingles or repairs anything. An automated assistant takes your call, gets a sentence about the roof and your town, and rings you through to a locally owned DFW roofer. Inspection, estimate, work and bill all come from that roofer. Roofers can owe the line a fee for each referral. The how it works page walks through a call.

How do I choose a roofing company in Dallas?

Start with paperwork, since Texas never licensed roofers: proof of liability coverage that comes to you from the insurance agent, a signed scope listing every material, the permit your city requires, and a few addresses of roofs the company finished nearby. Anyone offering to swallow your deductible is breaking state law, so move on. The guide on how to check a roofer in Texas covers each item.

What does it cost to use the line?

Nothing. The call is free, being connected is free, and the line never sends you a bill. The roofing company sets its own price for any work and should give it to you in writing before anything starts. Many roofers look at a roof at no charge, but not all do, so ask during the call. For what moves the price of a full re-roof here, read the DFW roof replacement cost guide.

Can I call in the middle of the night or right after a hailstorm?

Yes. The automated assistant answers around the clock, including weekends and the hours after a storm when everyone is calling. You are rung through to a DFW roofer; when no one answers there, the roofer still receives who you are, your number, your town and the problem, and calls back. Arrival times are up to that roofer and the sky. For water coming in right now, start with emergency roof repair and tarping.

Which towns can call the line?

All of Dallas-Fort Worth: Dallas, Fort Worth and the suburbs across Dallas, Tarrant, Collin, Denton, Rockwall, Kaufman, Ellis, Johnson, Parker and Hood counties. Sixty-seven towns get a page of their own covering city permits and past storms, from Denton and Celina in the north to Waxahachie, Cleburne and Granbury in the south and west. The service areas page lists them all.

Roof problem anywhere in DFW? Call the free line

Say what the roof is doing and which town you are in. The automated assistant passes you to an independent roofing company that is locally owned and works in DFW. That company comes out, looks at the roof and prices the job itself.
